title: QUIC RFC 9000 Retry Client Processing and Replay Continuity Work Item
summary: Close the bounded RFC 9000 Retry client processing and replay-continuity gap by replacing broad placeholder proof with focused requirement-home tests and canonical trace links.
planned_changes:
- Add negative and edge tests for first-Retry acceptance, malformed Retry metadata rejection, duplicate Retry discard, Retry replay token and connection-ID use, source connection-ID preservation, Retry non-acknowledgment, ClientHello preservation, post-Retry 0-RTT destination selection, packet-number continuity, and protected 0-RTT payload confidentiality.
- Add support helpers for maximum-length Retry Source Connection IDs, minimum non-empty Retry tokens, Retry replay packet decoding, and server protection setup with non-default Retry values.
- Record focused architecture and verification ownership for S17P2P5P2 and S17P2P5P3 requirements that are proven by the managed client runtime and packet builders.
- Keep optional server abort behavior for detected packet-number reset out of scope because the repository does not currently prove that MAY behavior.
verification_plan: Run the focused S17P2P5P2/P3 requirement-home filter, rerun the S7P3 filter to guard the adjacent connection-ID closure, run a Release build, regenerate QUIC requirement coverage triage, validate SpecTrace JSON, run the full Release test suite without rebuilding, and check the resulting diff for whitespace errors.
out_of_scope: Optional S17P2P5P3-0008 server abort behavior for detected packet-number reset.
Public early-data APIs or application-level 0-RTT acceptance.
0-RTT anti-replay policy beyond packet protection of confidential payload bytes.
Retry token cryptographic envelope design outside the existing Retry packet integrity and token propagation floors.
completion_notes: Completed as a focused RFC 9000 Section 17.2.5.2 and 17.2.5.3 proof over client Retry packet acceptance, duplicate Retry discard, Retry-selected Initial replay, post-Retry 0-RTT destination selection, packet-number continuity, and protected 0-RTT payload confidentiality.
